precepts.text: I will bring the worst of the heathen and they shall possess their houses; mischief upon mischief and rumour upon rumour.
precepts.point: Thou shalt plant pleasant plants and set it with strange slips: a slip is a cutting from a plant, so strange branches, Esau, not the people of the covenant, set in the land.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the land would be set “with strange slips”, and Christ says Jerusalem would be “trodden down of the Gentiles.” Ezekiel gives another precept on who those strangers are.

“Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses.” God calls them the worst of the heathen, and they will possess our houses. Those are the Gentiles Christ was speaking about in Luke 21:24, the strange slips planted in our land.

“I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be defiled. Destruction cometh; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none. Mischief shall come upon mischief, and rumour shall be upon rumour.”

That is what we see now. America and Israel fund rebel forces and put a former al-Qaeda commander, Abu Mohammad al-Jolani, once with a ten-million-dollar bounty on his head, in as president of Syria, because Assad said they are not even real Jews and shouldn't be in the land; now Trump shakes his hand in the White House. Israel announces it will occupy southern Lebanon up to the Litani River. Mischief upon mischief and rumour upon rumour: the worst of the heathen possessing the houses of the children of Israel.

precepts.text: I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth.
precepts.point: There is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. Evil was among Israel before the white man; it only multiplied under him.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
Even in the Israelite nation you have evil ones. “As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty: but they made the images of their abominations and of their detestable things therein: therefore have I set it far from them.” We were sacrificing to idols, worshipping other gods and violating God's laws.

“And I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil; and they shall pollute it.” God gave our land and our sanctuary into the hands of other nations, starting with the Babylonians, and to the wicked of the earth: that is Edom, the European man. “My face will I turn also from them”: you ask for my help and I am not listening. “for the robbers shall enter into it, and defile it.” The robbers are still there; they call themselves Israelis today. Imagine a robber who robs your house and never leaves: he posts up, puts your ass in the basement, and when someone asks whose picture that is of a black man, he says, that's me, I had a tan that day.

“Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.” Make a chain means judgment was established. What is crime? Sin. We became a nation of criminals, and a criminal gets incarcerated; we are still serving our sentence today. Some will stay in prison till it burns, and some will get out on good behaviour, keeping God's commandments. Our cities were full of violence before any white intervention, and we are the answer to our own problems.

“Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses”: the worst of all the nations God made, and we are under him now. He possessed our lands, our people and our identity. “I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease”: we were prideful, sure nothing would happen to us and we would be in the land forever. “Destruction cometh; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none.” We seek peace, equality and rights, and there is none, because we were rebellious then and we are worse now.

precepts.text: Make a chain, for the land is full of bloody crimes; that is what came upon Jerusalem when this law was not applied among the people.
precepts.point: A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
This is what came upon Jerusalem when the witness law was not applied among the people. The Lord gave the city “into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil”, turned His face from them, and the robbers entered His secret place and defiled it.

“Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.” A land full of bloody crimes is a land where those who saw and knew did not utter it. When sin among Israel is hidden instead of brought out, the whole city fills with violence and the Most High hands it over.
